articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Discontinuous Conduction Mode Flyback LED Driver with Variable Compensation Circuits for Output Current Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Flyback converter is a type of isolated buck-boost converter where it uses a mutually coupled inductor to store energy in the magnetic field. Discontinuous conduction mode (DCM) is a process where the coupled inductor can demagnetize completely during each switching cycle. Compensation circuit with an error amplifier can help to improve the overall stability of the system by improving the phase margin. A flyback converter in discontinuous conduction mode with variable compensation design for LED driver is presented. This paper focused on the analysis to select the suitable compensation topology based on 2 main criteria: percentage of overshoot and settling time of output current when there are changes in the input voltage or LED threshold voltage. In this work, the LTspice program is used to simulate the transient response and MATLAB software to analyze the phase margin and crossover frequency of the open-loop transfer function of the flyback converter with compensation circuit. Based on the finding, type II compensation circuit can provide an optimum output response with a sufficient phase margin and crossover frequency.

articleTitle: Electrical Breakdown Properties of Calcium Zirconate-based Polyethylene Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Multi-element oxide-based nanofillers often possess favorable properties over single metal oxide-based nanofillers. In the current work, the effects of untreated calcium zirconate (CaZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) nanofiller on the thermal and breakdown behaviors of polyethylene (PE) nanocomposites were investigated. PE nanocomposites containing 0.5 wt%, 1 wt% and 3 wt% of untreated CaZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanofiller were prepared using a Brabender melt mixer. Thin-film samples with thickness 100 μm were melt-pressed at 170 °C using a hydraulic hot press. The melting behaviors of prepared samples were characterized using the differential scanning calorimetry. Meanwhile, breakdown testing was performed to analyze the dielectric strength of the samples. The results indicated that the addition of higher amounts of CaZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> lowered the breakdown strength of the resulting PE nanocomposites. The breakdown result would serve as a reference for future characterization of the dielectric properties of PE nanocomposites containing treated CaZrO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> nanofiller.

articleTitle: Wind Turbine Lightning Protection Receptor with Sharp Needles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Wind turbines, as a form of renewable energy, are often located in remote, open areas such as offshore locations, mountainous regions, and deserts, where they are susceptible to lightning strikes. The blades of a wind turbine are susceptible to damage from lightning strikes due to their large size and position as the highest point in the wind turbine structure. Previous research focused on the size and location of receptors. Despite implementing a lightning protection system, it is not always effective in preventing lightning strikes on a wind turbine. Instead, other parts of the turbine may be struck, resulting in catastrophic damage to the equipment. From a technical perspective, using sharp needles as part of a lightning protection system can act as a lightning rod, drawing the electrical charge from a lightning strike and redirecting it away from the equipment, thus decreasing the potential for damage to the structure. Use 0.2m receptor size with two different numbers of needles, 16 and 32. The result obtained using the Finite Element Method showed a good result compared to the receptor without needles. It was observed through modelling that, when utilizing a receptor with 32 needles, the electric field measured was 3.69 MV/m, whereas when using a receptor with 16 needles, the electric field measured was 2.2 MV/m.

articleTitle: Proposed Single DC-Source High Gain SC-MLI Topology for Medium and High Power Drive Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The key benefits of multilevel inverters include higher efficiency, higher power density, and improved power quality, making them a viable option for this application. The proposed Switched capacitor multilevel inverter topology requires thirteen unidirectional switches, one bidirectional switch, a single DC voltage source, and four capacitors for obtaining the 17-level output voltage with quadruple voltage boosting ability. The capacitor's voltages are self-balanced, reducing the complexity of circuits and eliminating the requirement for additional circuits or sensors. The proposed topology's feasibility is examined under fixed and dynamic loads. The PLECS software is employed to determine the losses across the components. The proposed topology has an efficiency of over 97% and can generate 17 levels of 4.86% total harmonics distortion (THD).

articleTitle: Enhancing the Breakdown Strength of PP/EPDM Blend: The Role of PP-g-MAH Compatibilizer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: In pursuit of environmentally sustainable electrical insulation materials, the current study examines the potential of a blend of polypropylene (PP) and ethylene propylene diene monomer (EPDM), compatibilized with maleic anhydride-grafted polypropylene (PP-g-MAH), to overcome the brittleness of standalone PP and improve the overall material properties. The dielectric breakdown strength of the PP/EPDM blend containing 1 wt%, 3 wt%, and 5 wt% of PP-g-MAH was evaluated and compared against the conventional cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE). The breakdown test method adheres to the American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D3755 standard, with the breakdown strength quantitatively analyzed using the Weibull statistical method. The results indicate that PP-g-MAH improves the compatibility and enhances the breakdown strength of the PP/EPDM blend, particularly at 5 wt% of PP-g-MAH concentration. The findings suggest that PP/EPDM blends optimized with PP-g-MAH are promising candidates for sustainable insulation applications, warranting further exploration into their potential to be used in power cable insulation.

articleTitle: An Improved Non-Isolated High-Gain Switched Capacitor and Inductor Based DC-DC Converter For EV Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: For grid-connected applications or high-power applications like fast charging of electric vehicles, high voltage sources were needed. Renewable energy sources (RESs) like fuel cells (FCs) or photovoltaic (PV) arrays necessitate raising the initially low input voltages. This paper presents an efficient high-gain, single-switched DC-DC boost converter using switched-inductor and switched-capacitor cells. The circuit is producing an improved output voltage with a gain of nine. By combining capacitors and diodes, switched-capacitor cells can provide additional voltage levels. The circuit is modelled and analyzed for both CCM and DCM operations. A comparison with other similar DC converter circuits is carried out to further verify the performance of the proposed circuit. High gain output with lower ripple and stresses makes the proposed converter circuit suitable for medium and high-power applications.

articleTitle: Harmonic Analysis in Grid-Connected Photovoltaic System Under Varying Solar Irradiance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: There has been a growth in the utilization of photovoltaic systems in the generation of electrical energy. These systems are used either as a means of supplying power in places where there is no grid connection, which is known as a standalone system, or by feeding electricity into the grid, which is called a grid-connected system. As the use of photovoltaic systems continues to grow, there is a possibility that the system could experience problems with its power quality. Total harmonic distortion (THD) is one of the power quality issues that becomes a serious concern in the system when photovoltaic (PV) is connected to the grid system. This research examines how solar irradiation variation affects the total harmonic distortion (THD) of current and voltage using a MATLAB Simulink model. The PV model developed is tested using three different conditions, which are low, average and high solar irradiance. According to the findings, lower levels of solar irradiance will have a significant influence on the rise in overall harmonic distortion of the current.

articleTitle: Distribution Transformer Losses Analysis due to Photovoltaic-Induced Current Harmonics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Harmonic distortion is one of the monumental power quality disturbances in an electrical distribution system, which originates from power electronic assets such as power electronic devices from consumers and renewable energy integration. Harmonics adversely affect distribution transformers by elevating losses in their components, leading to the reduction of their lifespan. The impact on the transformer losses is a crucial attention especially considering the integration of photovoltaic systems (PV) into distribution network. Therefore, this paper examined the relationship between current harmonics from various photovoltaic penetration towards load losses generated in an oil-immersed distribution transformer in three-phase distribution network with the presence of unbalanced harmonic loads. The simulation was carried out using MATLAB Simulink 2021a software, during which the current distortion was compared evaluated and compared in accordance with a specified standard. As a result, the rise in PV penetration has been demonstrated to lead to increased losses in distribution transformer.

articleTitle: Thermal Aging on Polypropylene/Magnesium Aluminate Nanocomposites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This research examines on the effects of thermal aging at 110 °C on pure polypropylene and polypropylene nanodielectrics containing magnesium aluminates with 1, 2, and 5wt%• Thermal, structure, and chemical properties of the samples were obtained using differential scanning calorimeter, scanning electron microscopy, and Fourier transforms infrared, respectively. The results show that the structure and chemical contents of aged PP and PP nanodielectrics was unaffected despite being subjected to aging. Besides, melting temperature of pure polypropylene and polypropylene nanodielectrics shifted by 1°C. Significantly, pure polypropylene experiences a 13% reduction after aging as compared to polypropylene nanodielectrics. Specifically, polypropylene nanodielectrics containing 1, 2, and 5 wt% of magnesium aluminates reduces by 1%, 3%, and 5%, respectively, after aging. This suggests that the utilization of magnesium aluminates nanofiller to polypropylene hinder the breakdown process after aging.

articleTitle: Simulation of Electric Field Intensity in XLPE Matrix with Different Voltage Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Electric power infrastructure in Malaysia faces a significant challenge with the use of Cross-Linked Polyethylene (XLPE) insulators, leading to internal partial discharges and potential breakdowns. This research addresses the problem by utilizing COMSOL Multiphysics software and Finite Element Method to simulate electric field intensity in XLPE matrix under varying voltages (15kV, 20kV, and 25kV), crucial for assessing cable aging. The study's field of inquiry encompasses the reliability and safety of power distribution networks, emphasizing on electric field intensity and potential without voids in XLPE matrix under different voltages. The methodology involves a step-by-step workflow using COMSOL Multiphysics 5.5 version software, employing a 2D approach to model electric field distribution in XLPE matrix. Findings reveal an inverse relationship between electric potential and gap length, highlighting the significance of gap spacing in mitigating electrical stress. The strongest electric field intensity occurs near the sphere electrodes, indicating potential locations for partial discharges.

articleTitle: Stand-Alone Microgrid Energy Distribution Through P2P Trading and Energy Storage Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading is an emerging solution for optimizing energy distribution in microgrids that requires utilization of local energy resources such as solar panels and energy storage devices. It is envisaged that energy networking will be capable of balancing energy locally and dealing with significant distributed energy resource (DER) penetration in the future. Adopting energy exchange technology in the microgrid system will develop a dynamic electricity market between peers and supplementing consumer needs with renewable energy sources. This study simulates a P2P energy trading system involving five houses, each equipped with solar panels, energy storage and loads. The objective is to identify sellers and buyers based on their current energy storage levels and calculate the amounts of energy to be traded. MATLAB software is used to simulate different patterns of consumption for every home over a 24-hour period. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of dynamically identifying sellers and buyers based on hourly energy storage levels. Houses with higher initial storage and energy generation during peak hours predominantly acted as sellers, while those with higher consumption rates were identified as buyers. The calculated amounts of energy to be sold and purchased were adjusted, ensuring accurate trading volumes that reflect the present energy supply and demand conditions. This practical simulation provides valuable insights in showcasing how energy can be efficiently distributed within a prosumer. The study contributes to the understanding of instantaneous energy trading mechanisms and highlights the potential for optimized energy management through P2P systems.

articleTitle: Impact of EV Charging Stations on Electrical Distribution System with PV System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The rapid growth in electric vehicle (EV) adoption necessitates the expansion of electric vehicle charging station (EVCS) infrastructure, posing challenges to electrical distribution systems. Photovoltaic (PV) systems offer a renewable solution to support the increased load from EVCS. This study analyzes the impact of EVCS on electrical distribution systems using the IEEE 33-bus model, considering residential and commercial load profiles. Comparative analysis between the base case and scenarios with EVCS shows that integrating PV systems improves voltage profiles, with commercial load bus 33 voltage increasing from 0.705 pu to 0.916 pu at 11:00 AM. To address evening voltage drops, the study recommends implementing energy storage systems (ESS) to store excess daytime solar energy. This research highlights the importance of integrating EVCS, PV systems, and ESS to enhance the performance and reliability of electrical distribution networks.

articleTitle: Analytical Solution of the Voltage Distribution Problem Along Insulator Strings of Nonuniform Disks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This paper deals with deriving the analytical solution to the problem of determining the voltage distribution along the suspension insulator strings composed of a mixture of clean and polluted nonidentical disks having nonuniform ground and line stray capacitances. A system of linear equations describing the voltage distribution was formed based on the insulator string equivalent lumped circuit and transformed into a tridiagonal matrix equation. Explicit recursive formulae for calculating the tridiagonal system matrix determinant, adjugate, and inverse were derived. Closed-form non-recursive formulae in terms of special second-order matrices for computing the entries of the adjugate or adjoint matrix were also obtained. Moreover, an alternative method for forming the tridiagonal system matrix adjugate and inverse matrix in terms of diagonal and triangular matrices and their transpose was developed. The said formulae enable one to calculate the string efficiency and the voltage distribution along the insulator string for the general case where nonuniformity of the disks and stray capacitances are imposed and different contamination levels are prescribed. The formulation approach to the problem and the analytical solution obtained admits the inclusion of tower design and environmental effects such as due to wind velocity and the use of corona rings and grading rings.

articleTitle: Enhancing Wind Turbine Blade Lamination with Nano Particles for Lightning-Resistant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Nanoparticles have emerged as promising agents for mitigating lightning protection on insulation surfaces, offering potential benefits for wind turbine blade design. This research investigates the integration of carbon nanoparticles into epoxy composites and fiber-reinforced polymers. Experimental findings demonstrate the effectiveness of nanoparticle doping in suppressing surface charge accumulation and enhancing insulation properties, such as flashover voltage and partial discharge. Wind turbines, composed of insulating materials, accumulate electrostatic charges during operation, posing a risk of lightning attachment. However, addressing the discharge of these charges remains understudied. Incorporating nano-composite materials into wind turbine blades presents an opportunity to improve breakdown strength and reduce corona generation. This project aims to assess the impact of fiberglass epoxy Nanocomposite on reducing the risk of lightning strikes on wind turbine blades through Finite Element Method simulations. Carbon Nano Tubes are selected as fillers based on their electrical conductivity and integrated into the blade structure to analyze their effect on electric field strength. Initial simulations reveal significant reductions in electric field distribution upon carbon nanotube integration, highlighting the efficacy of nanoparticle integration in mitigating surface charge accumulation and improving the electrical properties of insulating materials for high-voltage applications such as wind energy generation.

articleTitle: Breakdown Strength of Polypropylene Blended with Propylene-based and Ethylene-based Copolymers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Nowadays, thermoplastic polypropylene (PP) has been proposed as an alternative material for thermoset crosslinked-polyethylene (XLPE) in high voltage alternating current (HVAC) and high voltage direct current (HVDC) cable insulation applications. However, PP's mechanical tensile yield strength and elastic modulus are very high, and do not meet the criteria of power cable extrusion. Hence, elastomers have been blended with PP to improve the mechanical properties, even though this may negatively affect the breakdown properties of PP/elastomers blends compared to pure PP. In this paper, the DC breakdown performance of PP/elastomer blends containing 20 wt% of propylene-based copolymer (PBC) and ethylenebased copolymer (EBC) has been studied. The results demonstrate that PP blended with 20 wt% of PBC has slightly higher DC breakdown value (344 kV/mm), compared to the XLPE (324 kV/mm). Meanwhile, the DC breakdown value of PP blended with 20 wt% of EBC can be comparable (317 kV/mm) to XLPE. Therefore, from the perspective of DC breakdown performance, both PP/PBC and PP/EBC blends, when blended with 20 wt% of elastomers, can be good alternatives to XLPE.

articleTitle: Voltage Sag Mitigation Using DVR for Three-Phase Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: In contemporary industries, the reliable operation of sensitive process equipment is of paramount importance. Voltage dips, particularly voltage sag-a reduction in AC voltage lasting from 0.5 cycles to one minute-have emerged as a critical concern, causing operational disruptions and financial losses across various sectors. This phenomenon, attributed to factors such as faults and lightning strikes, significantly impacts power quality, particularly in three-phase systems. To address these challenges, Flexible AC Transmission System (FACTS) devices, such as the Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) equipped with a Proportional-Integral (PI) controller, offer promising solutions. This report discusses the effectiveness of DVRs with PI controllers in mitigating voltage sag due to three-phase faults. The issue at hand is voltage dips or sags, a common power quality concern for utility customers with sensitive process equipment. Voltage sag, which is defined as a drop in AC voltage for a period ranging from 0.5 cycles to 1 minute, is a serious problem for industries where even little fluctuations in voltage can result in expensive process downtime. When faults, lightning strikes, and other events have an adverse effect on line voltage and/or current waveforms, voltage sag appears as a three-phase phenomenon in three-phase systems, affecting both phase-to-phase and phase-to-ground voltages. To tackle these issues, FACTS devices have been introduced into electrical systems to mitigate voltage sag and enhance overall power quality. This paper aims to contribute to the existing body of knowledge by investigating the performance of DVR with PI controller in mitigating the voltage sag due to three-phase fault under varying active power ratings for balanced load.

articleTitle: Analysis of Paralleling Transformer with Different Topology Considering Single Phase to Ground Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The transmission transformer must continuously operate, and if one transformer trip due to a any fault, another transformer must cover to fulfill uninterrupted power (n-l criteria) to the load. Transformers play an important role in power utility as the core of the transmission system to change voltage level. Next, to ensure n-1 criteria are fulfill, transformers at the transmission substation design in parallel mode. Specific prerequisites need to be met to connect transformers in parallel. This study will focus on one parallel criterion: the transformer's topology or vector group. Typically, transmission substations are fit with two 132/22kV transformers of the identical YNd1 vector group. Then, to analyze the effect of paralleling two transformers with different topologies, two transformers of different vectors will be paralleled using MATLAB Simulink environment. This system will be simulated with a possible single phase to ground fault event. This analysis will advance to analyzing the network without an earthing transformer linked at the low voltage side of the 132/22kV transformer. The results will be examined the effect of single-phase fault at paralleling transformers with different topologies.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study of Initiation of Ferroresonant Modes of a Single-Phase Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This paper presents a study that simulates the initiation of various ferroresonant modes in a single-phase transformer. The research explores how transformer parameters change, employing a hysteresis core model that is adjusted across a wide range of grading and shunt capacitances. The adjustment process is influenced by the degree of core saturation. The study indicates that transformers with substantial core loss are effective in suppressing ferroresonance, suggesting this as a viable method for mitigating the occurrence of the ferroresonance phenomenon.

articleTitle: Hardware Implementation of Finite Control Set-Predictive Torque Control for Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Finite Control Set - Predictive Torque Control (FCS-PTC) has become a popular control algorithm for induction motor (IM) drives for the past few decades. However, selecting the best weighting factor (WF) to provide optimal IM performance is challenging and has become the main disadvantage of FCS-PTC. Therefore, this paper introduces a real-time adjustment WF for the FCS-PTC using a flux controller (FC). The FC is represented as a scheduled DC gain and is designed to be proportional to the absolute value of the predicted stator flux error. This method eliminates the need for complex computation to select the appropriate WF and efficiently regulates the flux and torque. An experimental validation using a DS1104 controller board was conducted to compare the proposed method with FCS-PTC that uses a constant flux WF method (specifically WF value of 30), tested with a wide range of motor speed conditions. The results confirmed that the proposed method outperforms other methods in regulating torque and flux response.

articleTitle: PV-Based Water Pumping System for Oil Palm Irrigation in Malaysian Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Conventional diesel-driven water pumping systems have been widely used for irrigation purposes, but they present drawbacks such as high operational costs and significant environmental harm. This paper examines the design and performance of a proposed PV-based water pumping system for oil palm irrigation under Malaysian conditions. To design the proposed system, several parameters need to be calculated such as water requirement, flow rate, total dynamic head, pump power, and PV output power. In this study, the calculated value will be validated and compared with the design suggested by the PVSyst software. It is an effective tool for modeling and analyzing the performance of the PV-based water pumping system. Therefore, the result is used to evaluate the potential of the proposed system in providing a sustainable irrigation solution. Serting Hilir was selected as a case study because this area is covered with palm oil plantations that require proper irrigation systems, especially during dry weather conditions. The result shows that the proposed PV system demonstrates satisfactory water pumping capability, achieving a cumulative water volume of 54,923 m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and an energy consumption of 13,730 kWh. Despite a 10.5% deficit in meeting water demand, the system exhibits a surplus of 27 kWh of energy and a total system efficiency of 76.1%.

articleTitle: Enhancing Energy Fraud Detection with Ensemble Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This study aims to enhance the detection of fraudulent energy consumption patterns by integrating advanced machine learning techniques and time series analysis to improve the accuracy and robustness of classification models. Previous approaches have struggled with challenges such as missing data, imbalanced class distributions, and high-dimensional time series analysis. To address these issues, the proposed method combines several advanced techniques: Multiple Imputation by Chained Equations (MICE) for imputing missing data, AdaBoost classifiers for balancing class distributions, Piecewise Aggregate Approximation (PAA) for reducing dimensionality while preserving key patterns, and Light Gradient Boosting Machine (Light GBM) for robust classification. This integrated approach significantly improves classification performance, achieving high accuracy (94%), precision (94.5%), and recall (93.18%), and offers a scalable framework for future research and practical applications in energy management.

articleTitle: Combined and Substituted Use of Battery Electric Vehicles and Hydrogen in Nanogrid Configurations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Renewable energy systems consider energy storage against uncertainties of weather resources and customer demands. Battery energy storage dominates recent renewable energy-based system developments. Factors for the battery dominance include the extended life-cycle, high energy density and low per unit kWh cost. However, hydrogen storage had a significant drop in per kWh cost and longer periods of energy storage. Electric vehicles have a high percentage of lifespan spent parking implying low energy storage usage. This paper investigates the technoeconomics of a residential nanogrid's energy storage system configured using battery, electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cells. The Photovoltaic/Wind/Storage nanogrid configurations were optimized using nested integer linear programming with energy storage planned in combined and substituted modes for cost/capacity benefits. The nanogrid's energy costs in substituted storage were 44%, 22% and 39% in battery, electric vehicles and hydrogen storage lower than the combined storage's 0.0018 $/kWh. The substituted storages are 30%, 24% and 44% lower than the combined storage's $111,330 annualized total cost. However, hydrogen storage's 65 kW capacity is larger compared to electric vehicle's 55 kW and battery's 50 kW. Electric vehicles are envisaged to have better economic advantages under optimal load management.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Bifacial Photovoltaic Thermal Systems in Environmental Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This study aims to assess the performance of bifacial photovoltaic thermal (B-PVT) systems under real environmental conditions, considering factors such as solar radiation intensity and fluid mass flow rate. Testing was carried out in the city of Bandung, Indonesia. Sensors were to measure PV surface heat, inlet and outlet temperatures of air entering the system, as well as sensors to determine environmental conditions such as solar intensity. From the results of these measurements, the data was processed to obtain the efficiency of the bifacial PVT. From tests with different <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\dot{m}$</tex>, namely 0.15 and 0.25 kg/<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$s$</tex>, total efficiency values of the bifacial PVT system varying from 36.13% to 88.45%. This difference shows the importance of air flow rate regulation in maximizing system efficiency. To guide the development of more optimal designs and anticipate system performance under varying operating situations, mathematical modeling and computer simulations may be used in future research steps.

articleTitle: Optimal Placement and Sizing for Distributed Generation based on an Improved Differential Evolution Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Various methods have been developed to optimize Distributed Generation (DG) placement and sizing in the power system network. While better advanced algorithms for DG optimization are being continuously developed, simpler general purpose metaheuristic algorithms that had been developed earlier in the past decade, particularly Differential Evolution (DE), should be reevaluated in term of its application for DG optimization. Despite DE simplicity and significant advancement, DE application in DG optimization study is still minimal. In this paper, an improved differential evolution algorithm for DG optimization for power loss minimization in IEEE-69 radial network has been proposed. And improve the population diversity significantly increase its capability of escaping local optima. The results show the proposed method had 84% success rate, a significant improvement from the other selected DE variants with success rate ranging from 16% to 54%. This finding concludes that the proposed method has high potential of escaping the local optima and consequently can minimize the number of the required runs to find the optimal solution.

articleTitle: Optimization Techniques to Minimize the Power Loss and Maintain Voltage Stability for A Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: An increasing number of developing nations across the globe have encountered an inevitable surge in the demand for electrical power. This surge, if left unaddressed, can lead to a deterioration of the voltage magnitude and a decrease in the overall stability of the power systems. Within this context, an approach to mitigate system losses explored in this study involves the strategic allocation of distributed generation (DG). The pivotal factors in this endeavor are the judicious determination of the optimal location and sizing of DG units. Failure to achieve the optimal distribution, sizing, and placement of grid-connected DG can result in either over-compensation or under-compensation in a loss mitigation strategy. This study has been done by a comprehensive comparative analysis of the efficacy of three optimization techniques which are Evolutionary Programming (EP), Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), and Hybrid Swarm Evolutionary Programming (HSEP), for their capacity to minimize power losses while simultaneously upholding voltage magnitude in power system. The assessment was conducted on two distinct power systems which are the interconnected IEEE-30. The HSEP algorithm stands out by notably reducing total active power losses compared to others. The voltage profile graph highlights all optimization techniques consistently maintain values ranging from 0.95 to 1.05 p.u, complying with ANSI C84.1 standards. Multiple meta-heuristic algorithms to address intricate and multifaceted problems more effectively. Such an approach is particularly advantageous when dealing with complex challenges that can benefit from the identification of various optimization strategies.

articleTitle: Analyzing Lightning Activity and Windstorm Characteristics in a Severe Tropical Thunderstorm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Malaysia, located near the equator, is characterized by its rainforests and frequent monsoons, which lead to strong winds and heavy rainfall. These conditions often result in intense thunderstorms marked by severe convection. This study examines the relationship between windstorms and lightning during a storm on 30th of November, 2022. Geographic information systems (GIS) were utilized to map the spatial distribution of lightning, with data provided by the Malaysia Meteorology Department (METMalaysia) and Tenaga Nasional Berhad Research (TNBR). The study recorded 512 lightning flashes, consisting of 2% positive cloud-to-ground (+CG) flashes, 76% negative cloud-to-ground (-CG) flashes, and 22% intracloud (IC) flashes between 15:00 until 18:30 coordinated universal time (UTC). Wind speeds ranged from 0.3 to 4.4 m/s, typical for Peninsular Malaysia. The analysis revealed a strong correlation between lightning occurrences and windstorms during the initial stage of the thunderstorm. However, during the mature stage, this correlation weakened, likely due to low wind speeds, atmospheric conditions, and geographical factors. In the dissipating stage, the windstorm data showed unusual results with two IC flashes. This research highlights the potential of using lightning activity to forecast severe weather, demonstrating a complex but significant relationship between lightning and windstorms.

articleTitle: Improve PV Microgrid Connected to Main Grid Using Hybrid Backstepping Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The demand for clean, green and sustainable energy requires the use of renewable energy sources, especially in the context of microgrids. Microgrids (MGs) represent an important type of electricity transmission and distribution that combines various renewable energy sources (RES) with modern control technologies. Photovoltaic (PV) is one of the main parts in most of MG structures which offer higher level of availability and are integrated with storage system increases its benefits. However, PV array is a nonlinear system particularly when it comes to efficiency and control of solar energy and that's leads to difficulties to consistently achieve the Maximum Power Point (MPP) and design complexity for optimizing the power output. During changes of irradiance, the linear MPPT algorithms will suffering slow response, inaccuracy and power oscillations. Therefore, proposed a hybrid backstepping algorithm (HBS) which is combining of advantages of linear with nonlinear MPPT algorithms such as Perturb and Observe (P&O) with Backstepping (BS) to maximize power generation from the PV system and to regulate system currents, demonstrating effective dynamic performance, contributed to improve regulation of the dc-link voltage, active and reactive powers, ensuring minimal losses, unity power factor (UPF) and reduced harmonic distortion content (THD) for optimal power quality. The Lyapunov approach is used to analyze the system stability. The performance is evaluated by using a MATLAB environment for three systems, proposed HBS shows better efficiency, THD and fast response to the changes in solar irradiation when using BS in PV and Grid sides comparing with other conventional types.

articleTitle: Rule-Based Energy Management Strategy using 2-State Level for Standalone Hybrid PV/Wind/Battery/Diesel System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: Installing a standalone system composed of renewable energy (RE) sources like photovoltaic (PV) and wind turbines (WT) offers a practical and affordable solution to electricity problems in remote areas. Nevertheless, the primary challenge in maximizing the output from PV and WT systems is the intermittency of their power generation. Batteries and non-RE sources are necessary to ensure a continuous power supply to the load. However, the concern lies in maximizing the utilization of renewable energy (RE) output while ensuring that the battery in the standalone hybrid system does not degrade rapidly. This is particularly significant due to the economic implications associated with battery degradation, which can affect the profitability of battery investments. Therefore, this paper proposes a rule-based Energy Management System (EMS) that considers battery degradation aspects for standalone hybrid systems, aiming to maximize RE self-consumption and minimize the use of non-RE sources. Energy from RE sources and the battery undergoes continuous monitoring and management in peak and off-peak modes. These modes employ varying Depth of Discharge (DoD) and State of Charge (SoC) levels for the battery. During peak load hours, the energy stored in the battery is efficiently utilized by expanding the SoC range. This extended SoC range is allowed exclusively during peak hours to mitigate accelerated battery degradation. Through the implementation of the proposed EMS, the expense associated with non-RE sources can be minimized.

articleTitle: Hybrid CNN-BiLSTM Model for Power Quality Disturbance Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: With the evolution of intelligent grid tech, the need for monitoring power quality has markedly risen, essential for the continuous functioning of the power grid. Addressing this matter, this research proposes a combined approach combining Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) with Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) networks. The model effectively catches spatial or temporary aspects of power quality disruptions using CNN and employs BiLSTM to document long-term or temporal aspects, thus creating a profound correlation between input and output sequences. By substantially decreasing reliance on conventional physical attributes, this technique markedly enhances the precision in detecting power quality anomalies. Crucially, this technique, independent of particular original samples and existing information, holds widespread applicability and is applicable in identifying patterns in various other intricate systems. Research on experiments indicates that, as opposed to conventional machine learning frameworks, deep learning approaches are more effective in detecting disruptions in power quality. Our hybrid model excels in identifying power quality disturbance (PQD) and produces highly accurate recognition outcomes by autonomously analyzing central features of the disturbance indications.

articleTitle: Impact of Pole Height and Lamp Power on the Performance of Solar-LED Street Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: This paper focuses on optimizing solar-LED street lighting systems for roads classified under Malaysia's ME2 lighting standard, with the aim of identifying the best combination of pole height and LED lamp power to ensure efficient lighting, excellent visibility, and low energy consumption. Through DIALux software simulations, various configurations were tested, including 8-meter and 10-meter poles paired with 60W, 80W, and 120W LED lamps. The results showed that an 8-meter pole with an 80W LED lamp offers the best balance, achieving an average illuminance of 48 Lux near the poles, with an overall uniformity of 0.5% and longitudinal uniformity of 0.54%, which are crucial for consistent light distribution. This setup also demonstrated cost-effectiveness with an energy consumption of 320 kWh per year, making it ideal for urban and suburban areas with moderate to high traffic. In comparison, higher wattages or taller poles, such as a 120W LED on a 10-meter pole, provided increased brightness but led to reduced uniformity and higher energy costs, with power density rising from 0.017 to 0.020 W/lx-m<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. This research provides useful information for urban planners and engineers who seek to install efficient and effective solar-LED street lighting systems, thus contributing to sustainable urban growth.

articleTitle: Microgrid Reliability Assessment: Failure Event and Survival Profile Using Kaplan-Meier Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The growing integration of microgrids highlights the crucial necessity for in-depth assessments of component reliability to guarantee energy resilience and operational effectiveness. This study uses Kaplan-Meier survival analysis to evaluate the reliability of key microgrid components: batteries, photovoltaic panels, and fuel cells. This study aims to understand the survival profile of microgrid components, forecasting their failure event occurrences, and contrasting their potential reliability. Detailed power output data was gathered over a month from a microgrid, and survival probabilities were generated for each component. After defining the state of failure, the survival curves deliver a statistical bases for evaluating the operational reliability of each component. Results show distinct survival profiles for each component. Batteries and PV panels have high reliability for an extended duration but followed by a sharp decline, while fuel cells show a gradual decrease in survival probability from the beginning. These results imply that while batteries and PV panels are likely to function optimally until a critical failure point, fuel cells may necessitate more frequent maintenance due to their consistent decline. It is important to understand these degradation patterns to optimize maintenance timetable and refining the overall structure and functionality of microgrid systems. These findings offer a direction for future microgrid configuration and the establishment of predictive maintenance and replacement strategies that improve sustainability and operational stability in decentralized energy systems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Electric Vehicle Integration into the Power Grid: A Study of V2G Potential in Selangor, Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: The competition among ASEAN nations in the electric vehicle (EV) sector is escalating, with countries continuously refining their EV development strategies. In Malaysia, the adoption of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has been gradually gaining attention. However, the unregulated charging of large-scale EVs poses significant challenges to the stability and safety of the power system. While several studies have made progress in addressing individual EV-related issues, their optimization outcomes are limited and fail to meet actual requirements. Thus, a comprehensive study is essential to examine the impact of EVs on the grid and conduct multi-objective optimization. This research focuses on private EVs in Selangor, Malaysia, introducing an unprecedented case study for Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) implementation in the region. It commences with an analysis of factors influencing EV charging loads and the establishment of an EV charging load model. Multi-objective optimization is then applied to the Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) model to counter the adverse effects of widespread EV charging. The outcomes hold implications for optimizing charging costs and reducing peak power consumption on the grid.

articleTitle: Microgrid System Modelling for Hybrid Renewable Energy Market in Malaysia
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: A growing concern over climate change and the depletion of conventional energy resources have led to the urgent need for sustainable and resilient energy solutions. Previous studies, microgrid sizing only focusing on islanded mode and have limited global exploration. In comparison, various studies try to consider the microgrid (MG) in the grid-connected mode. Due to this need, this paper presents an innovative approach to MG system modelling, focusing on grid-connected with hybrid renewable energy sources (HRES) configurations in Malaysia landscape combining photovoltaic (PV), small hydropower (SHP), Biomass (BM), diesel generator (DG) and battery energy storage system (BESS). Our research aims to address the growing need for sustainable and efficient energy management strategies in the context of evolving energy markets. We have conducted a comprehensive performance analysis comparing various system modelling in microgrids connected to the distribution network, accounting for the uncertainties inherent in HRES. The design and performance analysis of the proposed multi-objective optimization algorithm is tested on the IEEE-33 Bus Distributed System. The findings are anticipated to contribute significantly to the development of sustainable energy solutions in Malaysia, offering insights for policymakers and stakeholders in the renewable energy sector.

articleTitle: Analysis and Evaluation of an Off-Grid Mini-Grid PV System for Rural Electrification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Advanced Power Engineering and Energy (APEE)
abstract: In recent years, there has been a growing interest in using renewable energy sources to electrify rural areas in Nigeria. The major motivation for this study is the recognition of the huge potential of renewable energy to improve rural electricity access in the country. One promising option is to use off-grid photovoltaic (PV) mini grid systems. These systems are small, modular, and can be easily installed in remote areas. However, some studies have shown that these systems are posed with certain problems such as its inability to carry loads for prolonged periods of time when the sun is out. This work investigates the feasibility of an optimized off-grid PV mini grid system for electrification of rural areas in Nigeria. The paper made use of the HOMER pro, SAM and MATLAB software. The HOMER pro software was to design a proposed mini grid for a case community in the northern part of Nigeria. The results of the HOMER pro simulations showed that the system generated high NPC and low LCOE. The proposed system for the northern generated an NPC of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}\!\!\!\!\!\!{=}$</tex>380,498,512 and an LCOE of 37.01<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}\!\!\!\!\!\!{=}$</tex>/kWh. The results of the SAM software showed that the PV array of the proposed models was able to generate sufficient electricity for the community. The results of the MATLAB software showed that a short-term load forecasting carried out using the ANN Levenburg-Marquardt algorithm gave results more accurately for the short-term load demand of the community. This exchange rate at the time of this work was <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{N}\!\!\!\!\!\!{=}$</tex>769.5 to $1.
